Tables and Access Groups ​

Every record lives in a table, in one access group. There is no schema to set up: a table is created by its first record and goes away when its last record is deleted.

A table is always written as an object with its name and its access group:

swift
["name": "posts", "access_group": "public"]

Table names are 1 to 256 characters long, with no control characters. /, !, *, # and % count as 3 characters each.

WARNING

Writing the table as a plain string, "table": "posts", is deprecated in getRecords and deleteRecords. It still means the public records of that table. Always write ["name": ..., "access_group": ...].

Access groups ​

access_groupSame asWho can read the records
"public"0Anyone, signed in or not.
"authorized"1Any signed-in user.
2 to 98Users whose own access group is that number or higher.
"admin"99Admins and the project owner.
"private""*"The uploader, and the users they grant access to.

A user reads records in access groups up to their own, which is the access_group in their profile (await skapi.user?["access_group"]?.int). The project owner sets it on skapi.com. Records come back with "public", "authorized", "admin", "private" or the number.

One table can hold records in several access groups. A query reads one table in one access group at a time:

swift
import Skapi

let skapi = try Skapi(projectId: "<Project ID>")

let publicNotes = try await skapi.getRecords(["table": ["name": "notes", "access_group": "public"]])
let memberNotes = try await skapi.getRecords(["table": ["name": "notes", "access_group": "authorized"]])

Who can write ​

Signed-out callers can create records in "public" only, and must write "access_group": "public" (or 0). Otherwise:

They try tocodemessage
name another access groupINVALID_PARAMETERUnsigned users have no access to records with access group.
leave access_group outINVALID_REQUESTPublic users can only post records to public tables.
update a recordINVALID_REQUESTPublic users cannot update existing records.
set a unique_idINVALID_REQUESTPublic users cannot set unique_id for records.
remove filesINVALID_REQUESTPublic users cannot remove files from records.

They cannot delete records either: deleteRecords needs a signed-in user. A record they create has a user_id that starts with anonymous:. It is temporary and names no user.

Signed-in users can post records to any access group up to their own, and to "private". They can update and delete only their own records, and not read-only ones. Admins can delete any record.

Reading while signed out ​

A signed-out caller can read only "public" records. Naming any other access group throws INVALID_PARAMETER: Unsigned users have no access to records with access group.

Require Login ​

When the project's Require Login setting is on (in the project settings on skapi.com), getRecords refuses signed-out callers before anything is sent:

swift
do {
    let posts = try await skapi.getRecords(["table": ["name": "posts", "access_group": "public"]])
} catch let err as SkapiError where err.code == "REQUIRE_LOGIN" {
    print("Sign in first")
}

The message is This project requires users to sign in before reading its database, so "getRecords" is not available to a signed-out visitor. Signed-in users are not affected, and neither are getTables, getTags, getIndexes and getUniqueId. The setting is a guard in the SDK, not an access rule on the server: data that must stay hidden from signed-out callers belongs in an access group above "public".
